problem: Zero-shot object navigation with LLM planners relies on static one-shot inference and struggles with ambiguous or partially observable scenes and conflicting perception.
motivation: Single-model perception and planning is brittle when observations are ambiguous or perception conflicts arise. Multiple specialized VLM experts that debate, supervised by an LLM controller, may give more robust and interpretable decisions for long-horizon zero-shot navigation.
key_idea: A central LLM controller supervises multiple role-specialized VLM experts (detection, risk assessment, spatial reasoning) that hold structured multi-round debates on perception conflicts, and the controller arbitrates the final action.
insight: Per the abstract, ablations reportedly confirm that the expert debate, multi-modal fusion, memory system and LLM arbitration each contribute. Only the abstract was available, so specific ablation numbers and details are unknown.
method: Multi-VLM expert debate: each VLM has a distinct role (object detection, risk assessment, spatial reasoning) and they engage in structured multi-round debates when perception conflicts arise
LLM controller: performs task decomposition, memory-guided exploration, and final arbitration based on expert arguments
Multimodal image fusion: combines RGB, depth and segmentation inputs to enhance perception
Map memory and trajectory tracking: avoids redundant exploration and supports long-horizon planning

setting.backbone: LLM controller plus multiple VLM experts (specific models not stated in abstract; presumably frozen)

numbers.eval_set_note: subset of HM3D with approximately 5,000 tasks
numbers.extra: strict zero-shot; split name not specified in abstract
numbers.evidence: Abstract: 'evaluated on a subset of the HM3D dataset with approximately 5,000 tasks, achieving a 52.3% success rate and 15.5 SPL under strict zero-shot conditions'

numbers_note: abstract only; split name uncertain, baseline numbers not available
results: DebateNav reaches 52.3% SR and 15.5 SPL on an approx. 5,000-task HM3D subset under strict zero-shot conditions, and is claimed to outperform several recent baselines. The SPL is low relative to SR, suggesting long paths.
limitations: Evaluated on a subset of HM3D rather than the standard benchmark split, limiting comparability
Multi-round multi-VLM debate likely adds heavy inference cost and latency
SPL is low (15.5) compared with SR, indicating inefficient paths
